status_legend.checked: Seen on a primary index, proceedings, publisher or arXiv page in some session; the URL is recorded
status_legend.checked-repo: Checked against the full text in an earlier session; see the explorations/ documents
status_legend.from-memory: Cited from knowledge; details not re-checked. Verify before quoting
status_legend.unverified: Cited by an author-supplied draft; not checked
status_legend.not-found: Searched for and not found on any primary index

meta.annotation_style: One to three sentences: what it shows, and what it does for the spine. 'supports'/'challenges' list claim IDs from claims.json or the GM/outline ID spaces (GM-T*, GM-C*, OUT-S*).

entries.title: Distributional Structure
entries.annotation: Original statement that linguistic meaning is reflected in distribution. The conjecture the spine treats as retrospectively verified (D1).

entries.title: A Synopsis of Linguistic Theory 1930-1955
entries.annotation: 'You shall know a word by the company it keeps.' Paradigm case of retrospective verification and of a sleeping beauty woken by a late hub (word2vec).

entries.title: Cours de linguistique generale
entries.annotation: Meaning as a system of differences. Embedding geometry is structuralism quantified (D2).

entries.title: Neural Word Embedding as Implicit Matrix Factorization
entries.annotation: Skip-gram with negative sampling factorizes a shifted PMI matrix. First rigorous geometry-from-co-occurrence theorem; the formal verification of Firth.

entries.authors: Arora, S.; Li, Y.; Liang, Y.; Ma, T.; Risteski, A.
entries.title: A Latent Variable Model Approach to PMI-based Word Embeddings
entries.annotation: Text generated by a slow random walk of a latent discourse vector; PMI geometry follows. Closest existing template for K1's latent-world-state model.

entries.authors: Karkada, D.; Korchinski, D.; Nava, A.; Wyart, M.; Bahri, Y.
entries.title: Symmetry in language statistics shapes the geometry of model representations
entries.annotation: Translation symmetry in co-occurrence forces Fourier geometry (circles for months, etc.). Anchor of the symmetric sector.

entries.title: Group-Invariant Statistics Determine Embedding Geometry
entries.annotation: Extends Karkada to finite and compact groups via harmonic analysis.

entries.authors: Huh, M.; Cheung, B.; Wang, T.; Isola, P.
entries.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
entries.annotation: Representations converge across models and modalities. The spine reads this as delta->0 and asks whether G rises (convergence) or falls (collapse).

entries.authors: Roeder, G.; Metz, L.; Kingma, D. P.
entries.title: On Linear Identifiability of Learned Representations
entries.annotation: Discriminative models including next-token predictors are identifiable up to linear transformation.

entries.authors: Marconato, E.; Lachapelle, S.; Weichwald, S.; Gresele, L.
entries.title: All or None: Identifiable Linear Properties of Next-token Predictors in Language Modeling
entries.annotation: Linear properties hold in all or none of distribution-equivalent predictors. Formal partition of Quinean indeterminacy into determinate and indeterminate parts.

entries.authors: Park, K.; Choe, Y. J.; Veitch, V.
entries.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
entries.annotation: Formalizes concepts as directions. Complements identifiability results.

entries.authors: Shai, A. S.; Marzen, S. E.; Teixeira, L.; Oldenziel, A. G.; Riechers, P. M.
entries.title: Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry in their Residual Stream
entries.annotation: Transformers trained on HMM outputs linearly represent the mixed-state belief simplex. Strongest support for the sufficiency lemma behind K1.

entries.authors: Xie, S. M.; Raghunathan, A.; Liang, P.; Ma, T.
entries.title: An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
entries.annotation: In-context learning as posterior inference over latent concepts.

entries.authors: Li, K.; Hopkins, A. K.; Bau, D.; Viegas, F.; Pfister, H.; Wattenberg, M.
entries.title: Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task
entries.annotation: Othello-GPT: board state recoverable and causally manipulable from move sequences alone. Synthetic world with known Omega.

entries.authors: Nanda, N.; Lee, A.; Wattenberg, M.
entries.title: Emergent Linear Representations in World Models of Self-Supervised Sequence Models
entries.annotation: Othello board state is linear when encoded relative to the current player.

entries.title: Language Models Represent Space and Time
entries.annotation: Linear probes recover geography and historical dates.

entries.title: Can Language Models Encode Perceptual Structure Without Grounding? A Case Study in Color
entries.annotation: Text-only color representations are roughly isomorphic to perceptual color space.

entries.title: Mapping Language Models to Grounded Conceptual Spaces
entries.annotation: Few-shot mapping of LM spaces onto grounded spatial and color domains.

entries.title: Harnessing the Universal Geometry of Embeddings
entries.annotation: Unsupervised translation between embedding spaces, suggesting shared geometry. Details not re-checked.

entries.title: Mind the Gap: Assessing Temporal Generalization in Neural Language Models
entries.annotation: Models degrade on post-cutoff text. Direct evidence of snapshot decay.

entries.title: Dated Data: Tracing Knowledge Cutoffs in Large Language Models
entries.annotation: Effective cutoffs differ from nominal ones and vary by resource. Supports the time-integrated composite.

entries.title: ChatGPT Is a Blurry JPEG of the Web
entries.annotation: Snapshot-as-lossy-compression intuition in public discourse.

entries.title: The Symbol Grounding Problem
entries.annotation: How can symbols mean without grounding? Spine reframes as state (possible) vs process (impossible) - GM T8+T2.

entries.title: Minds, Brains, and Programs
entries.annotation: Chinese Room. Targets understanding, which the spine explicitly does not claim.

entries.title: Climbing towards NLU: On Meaning, Form, and Understanding in the Age of Data
entries.annotation: Octopus argument: meaning requires communicative intent. Bounds K1 to world models, not meaning.

entries.authors: Bender, E. M.; Gebru, T.; McMillan-Major, A.; Shmitchell, S.
entries.title: On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots
entries.annotation: Source of 'stochastic parrot'; the spine turns it on humans (stochastic repeaters).

entries.title: Meaning without Reference in Large Language Models
entries.annotation: Conceptual role can carry meaning without reference.

entries.title: The Vector Grounding Problem
entries.annotation: Distinguishes kinds of grounding; argues referential grounding can be causal-historical.

entries.title: Do Language Models' Words Refer?
entries.annotation: Externalist argument: LM inputs have natural histories that can link words to the world. Answers Swampman; the snapshot is that natural history frozen.

entries.title: Word and Object
entries.annotation: Indeterminacy of translation; formalized by identifiability classes.

entries.title: Two Dogmas of Empiricism
entries.annotation: Blurs analytic/synthetic; reappears as the difficulty of bounding the reasoning gap.

entries.title: Philosophical Investigations
entries.annotation: Meaning as use; LLMs as use-machines (D6).

entries.title: The Meaning of 'Meaning'
entries.venue: Minnesota Studies in the Philosophy of Science 7
entries.annotation: Externalism; division of linguistic labor (elm/beech). Individuals are repeaters; reference is social.

entries.title: Naming and Necessity
entries.annotation: Causal chains of reference; the corpus as reference-transmission chain whose decay is collapse.

entries.title: Knowing One's Own Mind (Swampman)
entries.annotation: A historyless duplicate has no meaning. Mandelkern & Linzen argue LMs are not swampmen.

entries.title: Three Varieties of Knowledge
entries.annotation: Triangulation: objectivity needs two interpreters and a shared world. delta->0 collapses the triangle.

entries.title: Language, Thought, and Other Biological Categories
entries.annotation: Content depends on selection history: semantics is itself stateful.

entries.title: How to Make Our Ideas Clear
entries.annotation: Truth as the end of inquiry: convergence on Omega, contrasted with collapse onto each other.

entries.title: Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature
entries.annotation: Anti-representationalism: challenges the realist Omega the spine presupposes. Converted into the testable 'outside-text' falsifier.

entries.title: Of Grammatology
entries.annotation: 'Il n'y a pas de hors-texte.' If true, G is undefined; the spine makes this empirically contestable.

entries.title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
entries.annotation: Paradigm shifts; recognition depends on W changing. Cross-model alignment as a measure of commensurability (D17).

entries.title: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding
entries.annotation: No knowledge of matters of fact without experience; reductionism about testimony.

entries.title: Testimony: A Philosophical Study
entries.annotation: Anti-reductionist epistemology of testimony; LLM as pure testimony reasoner (D7).

entries.title: Learning from Words
entries.annotation: Testimony can generate knowledge the speaker lacks: a challenge to strict transmission views, relevant to aggregation and transcendence (debate D7).

entries.title: Epistemic Vigilance
entries.annotation: Humans filter testimony cheaply. Spine: vigilance checks against prior, not Omega.

entries.title: Not Born Yesterday
entries.annotation: Humans are not gullible. Counterweight to 'stochastic repeaters'.

entries.title: The Misunderstood Limits of Folk Science: An Illusion of Explanatory Depth
entries.annotation: People overestimate their understanding; knowledge is held communally.

entries.title: The Knowledge Illusion
entries.annotation: Community of knowledge; individuals as low-verification repeaters.

entries.authors: Bikhchandani, S.; Hirshleifer, D.; Welch, I.
entries.title: A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades
entries.annotation: Rational agents ignore private signals and cascade; fragile and possibly wrong.

entries.title: Naive Learning in Social Networks and the Wisdom of Crowds
entries.annotation: DeGroot learning converges to truth only if no agent has outsized influence. Hubs break the wisdom of crowds.

entries.title: Essai sur l'application de l'analyse a la probabilite des decisions
entries.annotation: Jury theorem: independent voters aggregate; correlation breaks it.

entries.title: The Condorcet Jury Theorem, Free Speech, and Correlated Votes
entries.annotation: Correlated votes degrade aggregation.

entries.title: Groups of Diverse Problem Solvers Can Outperform Groups of High-Ability Problem Solvers
entries.annotation: Diversity trumps ability (contested by Thompson 2014).

entries.title: On Liberty
entries.annotation: Collision of opinions needed for truth; the spine's migration term as Mill's argument with an equation (D11).

entries.title: Transcendence: Generative Models Can Outperform The Experts That Train Them
entries.annotation: Low-temperature sampling denoises across experts; requires delta>0 (independent errors).

entries.authors: Song, Y.; Zhang, H.; Eisenach, C.; Kakade, S.; Foster, D.; Ghai, U.
entries.title: Mind the Gap: Examining the Self-Improvement Capabilities of Large Language Models
entries.annotation: Self-improvement governed by the generation-verification gap; gap scales with pretraining compute; generation diversity degrades during iteration. The reasoning gap made operational.

entries.authors: Huang, A.; Block, A.; Foster, D. J.; Rohatgi, D.; Zhang, C.; Simchowitz, M.; Ash, J. T.; Krishnamurthy, A.
entries.title: Self-Improvement in Language Models: The Sharpening Mechanism
entries.annotation: Self-improvement as sharpening probability onto self-verified outputs. Redistributes existing mass, adds no G; formally a mode-ward drift (pulp mechanism).

entries.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
entries.annotation: RLVR wins at pass@1 but base models win at large k; RL narrows the reasoning boundary; distillation adds knowledge. Near-direct test of closed-loop C2.

entries.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
entries.annotation: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not reliably help.

entries.title: Beyond Model Collapse: Scaling Up with Synthesized Data Requires Verification
entries.annotation: Verification as the condition for synthetic data to help. Cited via One Selection Law; title wording from memory.

entries.title: A General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm that Masters Chess, Shogi, and Go through Self-Play
entries.annotation: Unbounded self-improvement where the rules are a perfect simulator - a free channel to a formal Omega.

entries.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
entries.annotation: RL with verifiable rewards; verifiers as channels within math and code.

entries.authors: Shumailov, I.; Shumaylov, Z.; Zhao, Y.; Papernot, N.; Anderson, R.; Gal, Y.
entries.title: AI Models Collapse When Trained on Recursively Generated Data
entries.annotation: Tails vanish first; Gaussian variance collapses a.s. under replacement.

entries.title: Self-Consuming Generative Models Go MAD
entries.annotation: Without enough fresh data per generation, quality or diversity degrades; quality-seeking sampling accelerates diversity loss.

entries.title: On the Stability of Iterative Retraining of Generative Models on their own Data
entries.annotation: Stable if real-data fraction is large enough: bounds 'inevitability'.

entries.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
entries.annotation: Accumulating data bounds error; replacement grows it linearly. Fixes the regime C3 must state.

entries.title: A Tale of Tails: Model Collapse as a Change of Scaling Laws
entries.annotation: Collapse as scaling-law change driven by tail truncation.

entries.title: Strong Model Collapse
entries.annotation: Collapse persists unless synthetic fraction vanishes; GM predicts it vanishes under grounded filtering.

entries.authors: Kazdan, J.; Schaeffer, R. et al.
entries.title: Collapse or Thrive? Perils and Promises of Synthetic Data in a Self-Generating World
entries.annotation: Real+synthetic mixtures contain collapse.

entries.authors: Schaeffer, R.; Kazdan, J.; Arulandu, A. C.; Koyejo, S.
entries.title: Position: Model Collapse Does Not Mean What You Think (ICML 2026: Multiple Definitions & Unrealistic Assumptions of Model Collapse Distract from Real World Threats)
entries.annotation: Eight definitions of collapse across 28 papers; catastrophic predictions rely on data deletion; redirects to present diversity collapse. Forces K30 to be about latent diversity, with regime stated.

entries.title: The Curious Decline of Linguistic Diversity: Training Language Models on Synthetic Text
entries.annotation: Lexical, syntactic and semantic diversity decline across self-consuming generations.

entries.authors: Briesch, M.; Sobania, D.; Rothlauf, F.
entries.title: Large Language Models Suffer From Their Own Output: An Analysis of the Self-Consuming Training Loop
entries.annotation: Diversity declines across self-consuming generations.

entries.title: Model Collapse as Cultural Evolution
entries.annotation: Abstract checked: task-grounded filtering sustains compositionality across self-training generations; random filtering does not. Full-paper numbers unverified.

entries.title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as a Rogers Chain
entries.annotation: Cited by One Selection Law; would directly instantiate K33. Must be checked before use (task Q-01).

entries.title: Data Feedback Loops: Model-driven Amplification of Dataset Biases
entries.annotation: Bias amplification in scrape-retrain loops tracks 'uniform faithfulness' of outputs to training distribution; proposes stabilization.

entries.title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
entries.annotation: Infinity-Chat (26K open-ended queries): intra-model repetition and inter-model homogeneity. Direct measurement that delta among models is small; ensembles less diverse than their count.

entries.title: Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity
entries.annotation: RLHF generalizes better than SFT but markedly reduces output diversity: alignment as a delta-reducing force.

entries.title: Does Writing with Language Models Reduce Content Diversity?
entries.annotation: Co-writing with InstructGPT (not base GPT-3) reduces cross-author diversity.

entries.authors: Wu, F.; Black, E.; Chandrasekaran, V.
entries.title: Generative Monoculture in Large Language Models
entries.annotation: Output diversity narrower than training data. Bibliographic details not re-checked.

entries.title: Algorithmic Monoculture and Social Welfare
entries.annotation: Shared algorithms can lower welfare even when individually more accurate.

entries.title: Picking on the Same Person: Does Algorithmic Monoculture lead to Outcome Homogenization?
entries.annotation: Shared foundation models homogenize outcomes.

entries.authors: Doshi, A. R.; Hauser, O. P.
entries.title: Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity but Reduces the Collective Diversity of Novel Content
entries.annotation: GPT-4 ideas raised individual story creativity (most for less creative writers) but made stories more similar: a social dilemma. Human-side co-collapse.

entries.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
entries.annotation: Excess-vocabulary method on 15M PubMed abstracts: at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts LLM-processed; effect larger than Covid. Omega (scientific writing) moving toward theta.

entries.title: Empirical evidence of Large Language Model's influence on human spoken communication
entries.annotation: 740K hours of talks/podcasts: abrupt rise of ChatGPT-preferred words ('delve') in speech after release; framed as start of a closed cultural feedback loop.

entries.title: Mapping the Increasing Use of LLMs in Scientific Papers / Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale
entries.annotation: LLM-modified text rising in papers and peer reviews.

entries.authors: Hao, Q.; Xu, F.; Li, Y.; Evans, J.
entries.title: Artificial Intelligence Tools Expand Scientists' Impact but Contract Science's Focus
entries.annotation: 41.3M papers: AI users publish ~3x more, ~4.8x citations, lead earlier; collectively topics shrink ~4.6% and scientist engagement falls ~22% ('lonely crowds'). Co-collapse in science. Numbers vary by version.

entries.authors: Perdomo, J.; Zrnic, T.; Mendler-Dunner, C.; Hardt, M.
entries.title: Performative Prediction
entries.annotation: Predictions shift the distribution they predict; performative stability and optimality. Formal home of Delta F = learn + perform.

entries.title: Performative Prediction: Past and Future
entries.annotation: Survey of performativity.

entries.title: An Engine, Not a Camera
entries.annotation: Black-Scholes changed option prices: the paradigm empirical case of performativity.

entries.title: The Looping Effects of Human Kinds
entries.annotation: Classifications change the classified: the reflexive part of Omega.

entries.title: The Self-Fulfilling Prophecy
entries.annotation: Self-fulfilling prophecy.

entries.title: How to Do Things with Words
entries.annotation: Performative utterances.

entries.title: Competing Technologies, Increasing Returns, and Lock-In by Historical Events
entries.annotation: Path dependence and absorbing states.

entries.title: The Ergodicity Problem in Economics
entries.annotation: Time averages differ from ensemble averages; corpus-as-ensemble vs life-as-trajectory.

entries.authors: Griffiths, T. L.; Kalish, M. L.
entries.title: Language Evolution by Iterated Learning With Bayesian Agents
entries.annotation: Chains of sampling Bayesian learners converge to the prior: collapse as the prior replacing evidence; genre formula as fixed point.

entries.authors: Kalish, M. L.; Griffiths, T. L.; Lewandowsky, S.
entries.title: Iterated Learning: Intergenerational Knowledge Transmission Reveals Inductive Biases
entries.annotation: Human function-learning chains converge to the inductive bias.

entries.authors: Kirby, S.; Cornish, H.; Smith, K.
entries.title: Cumulative Cultural Evolution in the Laboratory
entries.annotation: Iterated transmission makes languages more learnable and compressible.

entries.title: Demography and Cultural Evolution: The Tasmanian Case
entries.annotation: Small isolated populations lose cultural complexity. Human analogue of collapse; contested (Vaesen 2016).

entries.title: Population size does not explain past changes in cultural complexity
entries.annotation: Challenges Henrich-type demographic models; the spine's Ne-vs-census distinction may reconcile.

entries.authors: Cavalli-Sforza, L. L.; Feldman, M. W.
entries.title: Cultural Transmission and Evolution
entries.annotation: Foundational quantitative theory of cultural transmission.

entries.title: Culture and the Evolutionary Process
entries.annotation: Dual inheritance; conformist and prestige biases.

entries.title: Does Biology Constrain Culture?
entries.annotation: Social learning does not raise mean fitness at equilibrium in a changing environment. C2/C3 in evolutionary anthropology.

entries.authors: Enquist, M.; Eriksson, K.; Ghirlanda, S.
entries.title: Critical Social Learning: A Solution to Rogers's Paradox
entries.annotation: Copy, then check individually when copying fails: raises the verification threshold v*.

entries.title: The Cultural Origins of Human Cognition
entries.annotation: Cultural ratchet requires high-fidelity transmission.

entries.title: Evolution in Mendelian Populations
entries.annotation: Drift, effective population size, island model (F_ST ~ 1/(1+4Nm)).

entries.title: The Number of Alleles that Can Be Maintained in a Finite Population
entries.annotation: Infinite-alleles equilibrium heterozygosity 4N mu/(1+4N mu).

entries.title: Selforganization of Matter and the Evolution of Biological Macromolecules
entries.annotation: Error threshold: fidelity must exceed a length-dependent bound or information melts. Underwrites conservation pedagogy.

entries.title: Blind Variation and Selective Retention in Creative Thought
entries.annotation: Creativity as variation plus selection: genius and madness share variation, differ in selection.

entries.title: Exploration and Exploitation in Organizational Learning
entries.annotation: Fast socialization to the organizational code destroys the diversity the code needs; slow learners preserve it. C3, thirty years early.

entries.title: Designing Organizations for an Information-Rich World
entries.venue: Computers, Communications, and the Public Interest
entries.annotation: A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention: the filter moves to consumption.

entries.title: A General Theory of Bibliometric and Other Cumulative Advantage Processes
entries.annotation: Cumulative advantage in citation.

entries.title: The Matthew Effect in Science
entries.annotation: Credit accrues to the already credited.

entries.title: Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks
entries.annotation: Preferential attachment yields scale-free networks.

entries.title: Competition and Multiscaling in Evolving Networks
entries.annotation: Fitness x degree attachment: fit latecomers can overtake hubs.

entries.authors: Wang, D.; Song, C.; Barabasi, A.-L.
entries.title: Quantifying Long-Term Scientific Impact
entries.annotation: Citation dynamics via fitness, immediacy, aging.

entries.authors: Salganik, M. J.; Dodds, P. S.; Watts, D. J.
entries.title: Experimental Study of Inequality and Unpredictability in an Artificial Cultural Market
entries.annotation: MusicLab: social influence raises inequality and unpredictability; quality bounds but does not determine success.

entries.authors: Ke, Q.; Ferrara, E.; Radicchi, F.; Flammini, A.
entries.title: Defining and Identifying Sleeping Beauties in Science
entries.annotation: Beauty coefficient; sleeping beauties are not rare outliers.

entries.authors: Chu, J. S. G.; Evans, J. A.
entries.title: Slowed Canonical Progress in Large Fields of Science
entries.annotation: Larger fields concentrate citations on canon; new ideas cannot rise. Abundance entrenches the canon.

entries.authors: Park, M.; Leahey, E.; Funk, R. J.
entries.title: Papers and Patents Are Becoming Less Disruptive over Time
entries.annotation: CD index declines across fields; candidate signature of scientific collapse (contested methodologically).

entries.authors: Uzzi, B.; Mukherjee, S.; Stringer, M.; Jones, B.
entries.title: Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact
entries.annotation: Highest-impact papers: conventional core plus atypical combinations. Bibliometric 'surprising yet inevitable'.

entries.authors: Foster, J. G.; Rzhetsky, A.; Evans, J. A.
entries.title: Tradition and Innovation in Scientists' Research Strategies
entries.annotation: Risky innovation pays more but rarely; tradition dominates.

entries.authors: Sinatra, R.; Wang, D.; Deville, P.; Song, C.; Barabasi, A.-L.
entries.title: Quantifying the Evolution of Individual Scientific Impact
entries.annotation: Impact = Q x luck; Q stable over career; random impact rule. Careers as stationary generators.

entries.title: Hot Streaks in Artistic, Cultural, and Scientific Careers
entries.annotation: Hits cluster in hot streaks across domains.

entries.authors: Liu, L.; Dehmamy, N.; Chown, J.; Giles, C. L.; Wang, D.
entries.title: Understanding the Onset of Hot Streaks across Artistic, Cultural, and Scientific Careers
entries.annotation: Exploration followed by exploitation predicts hot-streak onset; neither alone does. Exploration = migration; exploitation = sharpening.

entries.authors: Kestemont, M.; Karsdorp, F.; de Bruijn, E.; Driscoll, M. et al.
entries.title: Forgotten Books: The Application of Unseen Species Models to the Survival of Culture
entries.annotation: Chao1 on medieval chivalric/heroic fiction: survival varies by tradition (English ~7% of manuscripts, Irish ~19%); low evenness (French) loses works. Archival tail loss.

entries.title: The Slaughterhouse of Literature
entries.annotation: Most published novels are forgotten; canon as selection.

entries.title: Distant Reading
entries.annotation: Quantitative literary history methods.

entries.title: Distant Horizons
entries.annotation: Predictive models of literary prestige; the empirical route to K45/K46.

entries.title: The Printing Press as an Agent of Change
entries.annotation: Print as a change in the conditions of replication and fixity.

entries.title: What Is the History of Books?
entries.annotation: The communications circuit: authors, printers, sellers, readers as a transmission network.

entries.title: Orality and Literacy
entries.annotation: Oral vs literate cognition and transmission.

entries.title: The Singer of Tales
entries.annotation: Oral-formulaic composition: the oral filter selects memorability.

entries.title: Literary History as a Challenge to Literary Theory
entries.annotation: Aesthetic distance from the horizon of expectations as value criterion; 'culinary' art requires no horizon change; distance fades for later readers. Precursor of K45-K48, including statefulness. (Concept checked via secondary sources.)

entries.title: Art as Technique
entries.annotation: Defamiliarization against automatized perception: escape from the prior.

entries.title: S/Z
entries.annotation: Readerly (consumed) vs writerly (reader produces): data vs program.

entries.title: Opera aperta
entries.annotation: The open work: high-entropy coherent interpretive distribution.

entries.title: Der Akt des Lesens (The Act of Reading)
entries.annotation: Gaps the reader fills: reader-dependent analytic residue.

entries.title: Is There a Text in This Class?
entries.annotation: Interpretive communities constitute texts' meanings; literariness as relation.

entries.title: Wahrheit und Methode
entries.annotation: Historicity of understanding; fusion of horizons.

entries.title: Pierre Menard, Author of the Quixote
entries.annotation: Identical text, different era, different meaning: fixed probe in changing Omega.

entries.title: Kafka and His Precursors
entries.annotation: Each writer creates his precursors: backward edges in the canon graph.

entries.title: Tradition and the Individual Talent
entries.annotation: Existing monuments form an ideal order modified by the new: retroactive canon.

entries.title: The Metaphysical Poets
entries.annotation: A hub redirects attention to Donne: revival by attachment.

entries.title: After Strange Gods: A Primer of Modern Heresy
entries.annotation: Includes Eliot's reserved assessment of Hopkins (tradition, range). Exact wording should be quoted from the scan.

entries.title: New Bearings in English Poetry
entries.annotation: Champions Hopkins: the hub that woke the sleeping beauty.

entries.title: Poems of Gerard Manley Hopkins
entries.annotation: Posthumous publication (poet d. 1889) via a friend who held the manuscripts: an archive of one.

entries.title: Beowulf: The Monsters and the Critics
entries.annotation: Reframed Beowulf from historical quarry to poem; Tolkien's fiction then amplified it. Single surviving manuscript (Cotton Vitellius A.xv), damaged in the 1731 fire.

entries.title: Why Read the Classics?
entries.annotation: 'A classic is a book that has never finished saying what it has to say.'

entries.title: Rereading
entries.annotation: Theory of rereading.

entries.title: Poetics
entries.annotation: 1452a: events contrary to expectation yet on account of one another.

entries.title: Republic, Book X
entries.annotation: Imitation thrice removed from truth: copies of copies (D10).

entries.title: Sein und Zeit, sec. 35 (Gerede)
entries.annotation: Idle talk: discourse passed along that has lost its referent. Operationalized as fluency stable while I(Omega;D) falls.

entries.title: Simulacres et simulation
entries.annotation: Precession of simulacra; fixed point of a self-consuming chain.

entries.title: The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction
entries.annotation: Reproduction and loss of aura; tail loss as loss of the particular.

entries.title: The Anxiety of Influence
entries.annotation: Strong poets misread precursors (clinamen): engineered latent diversity. GM's 'misprision'.

entries.title: Contingencies of Value
entries.annotation: Literary value is contingent.

entries.title: Cultural Capital: The Problem of Literary Canon Formation
entries.annotation: Canon formation as institutional (schooling) process.

entries.title: La Distinction
entries.annotation: Taste as social distinction; cautions against intrinsic value.

entries.title: Morphology of the Folktale
entries.annotation: 31 functions under surface variety: clowns in different makeup.

entries.authors: Reagan, A. J.; Mitchell, L.; Kiley, D.; Danforth, C. M.; Dodds, P. S.
entries.title: The Emotional Arcs of Stories Are Dominated by Six Basic Shapes
entries.annotation: Low-dimensional latent structure of narrative.

entries.title: Driven by Compression Progress
entries.venue: Anticipatory Behavior in Adaptive Learning Systems (LNCS 5499)
entries.annotation: Interestingness as first derivative of compressibility; formal basis for literature vs pulp.

entries.title: Logical Depth and Physical Complexity
entries.venue: The Universal Turing Machine: A Half-Century Survey
entries.annotation: Depth: computation needed to unfold structure; the analytic residue.

entries.title: Information Measures, Effective Complexity, and Total Information
entries.annotation: Effective complexity: length of the description of regularities.

entries.title: Aesthetic Measure
entries.annotation: M = O/C; earliest formal aesthetics.

entries.title: Aesthetics and Psychobiology
entries.annotation: Inverted-U of novelty and hedonic value.

entries.authors: Barron, A. T. J.; Huang, J.; Spang, R. L.; DeDeo, S.
